_comment: Guided tour of the Photon Table. 'name' is the emtk control (a spec action or field, or a window the app draws).

steps.title: What the file holds
steps.text: The file name, the number of photons (and of marker records besides them), the measurement time and the number of micro-time channels the header declares, then the records of each kind and the routing channels that occur in the data.

steps.title: Generate an example
steps.text: Load example writes a deterministic demonstration measurement (a µs-ALEX stream with bursts on two detectors) into the settings cache and shows its photons — no file of your own needed. Open TTTR... chooses a real .ptu, .ht3, .phu, .pt3 or other TTTR file instead; you can also drop one on the window.

steps.title: Move through the records
steps.text: A file holds millions of records, so the table shows one page. Next and Prev move by a page, First and Last jump to the ends. First record and Rows set the page by number.

await.hint: Press Next (it needs a loaded file with more than one page).

steps.title: Show one channel
steps.text: Pick a routing channel to keep only its records. The Record column then counts the filtered records while File idx keeps the position in the file.

await.hint: Choose a channel in the list.

steps.title: Photons or markers
steps.text: A scanning measurement interleaves the scanner's marker records with the photons. Kind keeps every record, only the photons, only the markers, or one marker kind (pixel, line start, line stop, frame, other) the file holds.

await.hint: Choose a kind in the list.

steps.title: The table
steps.text: One row per record: the index among the filtered records, the index in the file, the kind (each marker kind in its own colour), the routing channel, the micro time and the macro time in milliseconds. Click a header to sort the page.

steps.title: Copy the rows
steps.text: Copy visible puts the rows of the page on the clipboard as tab-separated text, with a header line.
